title: Daily Market Digest: Geopolitical Tensions Weigh on Indices Amid Fed Rate Hike Speculation
subtitle: September 8, 2026 - Shortened Trading Week Post-Labor Day

items.headline: U.S. Equities Dip as Geopolitical Concerns and Fed Outlook Dominate
items.summary: U.S. equity markets opened lower on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, after the Labor Day holiday, as heightened tensions in the Middle East drove oil prices higher, and Canada's retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods took effect. Major indices saw declines in early trading, continuing a cautious sentiment from Friday's close, influenced by recent strong jobs data and anticipated Federal Reserve actions.

items.headline: UBS Projects Two Fed Rate Hikes by Year-End
items.summary: UBS Global Wealth Management has revised its Federal Reserve forecast, now anticipating two 25 basis-point rate hikes in September and December. This shift follows a stronger-than-expected August jobs report and recent hawkish commentary from Fed officials, with CME FedWatch odds for a September hike reaching 58%. A closed meeting of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors is scheduled for today to review advance and discount rates.

items.headline: Manufacturing Sector Continues Expansion, Pace Slows
items.summary: The U.S. manufacturing sector expanded for the eighth consecutive month in August, though at a slightly slower pace, with the ISM Manufacturing PMI dipping 1.0 percentage point to 54.6%. Global manufacturing also strengthened slightly in August, driven by improved output and new orders, and a three-year high in employment.

items.headline: Energy and Information Technology Show Strength, Consumer Sectors Lag
items.summary: On September 8, 2026, a majority of S&P 500 sectors closed in negative territory. However, the Energy Select Sector SPDR ($XLE) rose 1.27%, and Information Technology showed a 0.45% gain. Conversely, Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ($XLY), Health Care Select Sector SPDR ($XLV), and Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ($XLP) were among the lagging sectors, falling 1.3%, 1%, and 1% respectively.

items.headline: United Natural Foods Reports Q4 Fiscal 2026 Results
items.summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. ($UNFI) today reported its fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results. The company saw a 0.7% decrease in net sales for Q4 compared to the prior year, while adjusted earnings per share for Q4 fiscal 2026 improved to $0.69 from an adjusted loss per share of $0.11 in Q4 fiscal 2025.

items.headline: Oil Prices Rise Amid Middle East Hostilities and Canada Trade Tariffs
items.summary: Global markets are reacting to escalating geopolitical tensions, with oil prices climbing due to heightened hostilities between the U.S. and Iran, including Houthi militant attacks on Saudi Arabian energy facilities. Additionally, Canada's retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods took effect, further contributing to market uncertainty.
